what_worked: Thorough caveats slide and consistent, clean visual design with honest missing-data callouts on most slides.
fix_next: Verify all computed figures against raw data; the $133.8M annualized total and mean MRR are materially wrong.
verdict: Clean-looking descriptive summary undermined by fabricated totals and no analytical depth.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2/12: $133.8M combined 12-month revenue not derivable from $15.6M dataset total. Slide 2: mean MRR $13,472 is ~10x too high. Slide 3: category median MRR values (AI $446, Marketing $1,586, Education $2,142) don't match reference medians. Slide 6: $0 bin shows 197 but reference has 216 zero-revenue rows.

evidence.insight: Every slide reports a single variable without combining dimensions; no correlation, segmentation, or cross-tab attempted. Takeaway restates slide 2.
evidence.narrative: Logical topic sequence (overview→categories→geo→audience→distribution→top10→growth→sales→payments→caveats→close) but no cumulative argument; each slide is a standalone fact card.
evidence.framing: Slide 11 caveats are thorough; missing-data noted on slides 3-4. But no stated audience or decision question; slide 5 omits 288 missing audience_type rows.
evidence.accuracy: $133.8M figure appears extrapolated rather than summed from data; mean MRR $13,472 inconsistent with $15.6M total; distribution bins suspiciously uniform and contradict 216 zero-revenue count; category medians deviate from reference.
evidence.visual: Consistent teal palette, direct-labeled bar charts, readable tables, good big-number callouts. Repetitive card template; slide 8 text-only where a chart would help.
evidence.ai_slop: Near-uniform bin counts on slide 6 look fabricated. Template repetition across slides 2, 8, 9. Structure resembles AI-generated executive summary with data plugged in.

change_reason: Downgraded accuracy from 4.0 to 3.5 after confirming the $133.8M figure is materially fabricated and distribution bins contradict known zero-revenue count; other scores confirmed as appropriate.
